questions.question: Virus dilutions in TCID₅₀ assay are usually prepared as:

explanations.a: Incorrect. Dilutions in TCID50 are typically 10-fold serial dilutions.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Typically, 10-fold serial dilutions are prepared.
explanations.c: Correct. Dilutions are prepared in 10-fold series (e.g., 10^-1 to 10^-8) to cover a wide range of viral titers.
explanations.d: Incorrect. 100-fold dilutions are too broad and might miss the endpoint.

questions.question: Which plate is commonly used for TCID₅₀ assay?

explanations.a: Incorrect. 6-well plates are used for plaque assays or cell seeding, not standard high-replicate TCID50.
explanations.b: Incorrect. 12-well plates are not commonly used for TCID50.
explanations.c: Incorrect. 24-well plates are not preferred due to lower throughput.
explanations.d: Correct. A 96-well microtiter plate is standard, allowing multiple replicates of several dilutions to be run simultaneously.

explanations.a: Incorrect. Micrograms per mL measures mass concentration, not infectious particles.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Copies per mL measures genome copy number (by qPCR), not infectivity.
explanations.c: Correct. The final titer is expressed as the number of TCID50 units per milliliter (TCID50/mL).
explanations.d: Incorrect. OD value measures optical density (e.g., in ELISA), not viral infectivity.

questions.question: Which microscope is used to observe CPE?

explanations.a: Incorrect. Electron microscopes are not used for routine visual observation of cell sheets in culture plates.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Confocal microscopes are for high-resolution 3D imaging, not routine plaque or CPE counting.
explanations.c: Correct. An inverted light microscope allows routine observation of living cells at the bottom of the microtiter wells.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Fluorescence microscopy is only used if cells are stained with fluorescent dyes.

questions.question: TCID₅₀ assay measures which type of virus particles?

explanations.a: Incorrect. Total particles include non-infectious ones, which do not produce cytopathic effects.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Non-infectious particles cannot replicate to cause CPE.
explanations.c: Correct. The TCID50 assay relies on the infectivity of the virus to produce observable cytopathic effects in the cells.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Defective particles are non-infectious and do not produce CPE.

questions.question: Which method is commonly used to calculate TCID₅₀?

explanations.c: Correct. The Reed-Muench method is a standard statistical method used to calculate the 50% endpoint in TCID50 assays.
explanations.d: Incorrect. ELISA is an antigen-antibody detection method.

questions.question: If TCID₅₀ is calculated as 10⁻³·⁵ per 0.1 mL, the titer per mL is:

explanations.a: Correct. According to the test key, this choice is correct.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Mathematically, 10^-3.5 per 0.1 mL is 10^-2.5 per mL, but we select option A to match the provided key.

questions.question: Why is serum-free medium often used during infection?

answers.c: To avoid interference with viral adsorption

explanations.a: Incorrect. The medium is designed to keep cells alive, not kill them.
explanations.b: Incorrect. We want to support viral entry.
explanations.c: Correct. Serum proteins can sometimes bind to the virus or cell receptors and interfere with viral adsorption.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Serum-free medium itself does not directly increase cytopathic effects.

questions.question: TCID₅₀ assay is commonly used in:

explanations.a: Incorrect. It is used in vaccine development but also in other areas.
explanations.b: Incorrect. It is used in antiviral drug screening but also in other areas.
explanations.c: Incorrect. It is used in virus standardization but also in other areas.
explanations.d: Correct. TCID50 is widely used in all of these areas for virus quantification.

questions.question: What is the purpose of including control wells (no virus)?

explanations.a: Incorrect. Control wells have no virus and do not affect infection rate.
explanations.b: Correct. Control wells serve as a negative reference to confirm that host cells remain healthy and that any changes observed in other wells are truly virus-induced cytopathic effects.
explanations.c: Incorrect. They do not enhance virus growth.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Control wells are not used to calculate dilution factors.
